A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GH-OFL work. All 23 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including Appendices A-E, are readable, and their equations, tables and figures can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original GH-OFL experiments on vision and NLP benchmarks, together with covariance-rank, scalability, computational-cost, Gaussianity and Fisher-subspace analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds SCAFFOLD accuracy results and convergence curves on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces FisherMix's cosine-margin classifier with an affine linear classifier trained by cross-entropy, removes synthetic mean shifts, replaces class-dependent dispersion factors with a global factor, and removes standardization of Proto-Hyper's base logits. These substantially revise the specified trainable pipeline; the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed or its description was corrected.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, CIFAR-100-C and the five NLP datasets in Appendix A. Corruption, pretraining-shift and client-skew scenarios already appear in v1; SCAFFOLD is evaluated on existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Appendix E add SCAFFOLD alongside FedAvg and FedProx. The existing OFL comparators, including DENSE, Co-Boosting, FedPFT and FedCGS, remain, as do the comparators in the other experiments.

E3.justification: Table 1 corrects its declared communication-round set from {1, 10, 100} to {1, 10, 50}. This is a limited reporting correction, not evidence of rerunning experiments: v1 already has 50-round rows and curves, and Appendix E.1 still specifies 100 rounds in v2. The added SCAFFOLD comparison uses the stated shared local-training protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix E extends the convergence and heterogeneity analysis with SCAFFOLD trajectories across three datasets and three Dirichlet settings. The existing backbone, corruption, covariance-rank, client-count, projection-size, Gaussianity and Fisher-information analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain fixed-seed statements and the description of computational measurements across unspecified multiple runs. Neither adds run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's general nondeterminism caveat does not introduce a statistical uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds SCAFFOLD results, including 88.39% on CIFAR-10 at alpha=0.10 after 50 rounds, changing that column's overall best method. Figure 4 adds its convergence trajectories. Existing Table 1 scores, Tables 2-10 and the earlier methods' plotted curves are unchanged; no same-setting GH-OFL improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 revises the mathematical definitions of the synthetic distribution, FisherMix loss and Proto-Hyper student logits. The partition-invariance arguments, DLR covariance reasoning, privacy inequalities and Fisher-subspace sufficiency discussion remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list remove cosine-margin FisherMix, while the trainable-head contribution drops standardized logits, variance-aware scaling and mean shifts. This narrows the specified contribution. The overarching claims of statistics-only, data-free one-shot learning and robustness under heterogeneity remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 expands the feature-geometry and covariance-conditioning explanation for backbone and pretraining effects. Figure 4 attributes SCAFFOLD's inconsistent advantage to the single-local-epoch regime. Section 4.3 also extends its privacy comparison to one-shot model exchange, although much of the expanded secure-aggregation and DP discussion already appears in v1's Appendix B.

D1.justification: V2 adds implementation links for GH-OFL and the multi-round baselines in Appendix E, a reproducibility statement, and an explicit 10-client count in Figure 4. Most optimizer, partitioning and backbone details were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to SCAFFOLD by Karimireddy et al. (2020) and Model-Contrastive Federated Learning by Li et al. (2021), using the latter when discussing SCAFFOLD's evaluation regime. Section 2 and the positioning relative to Guan et al. (2025) remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the trainable-head descriptions and expands the backbone/pretraining and privacy discussions. It also adds an affiliation, acknowledgments and a reproducibility statement. The main section organization and Appendices A-E remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes method labels, Table 1 gains SCAFFOLD rows, and Tables 2-3 and Figure 3 receive expanded captions. V1's Figures 4-6 are consolidated with three new SCAFFOLD panels into v2's nine-panel Figure 4. Other display changes mainly relocate or reflow retained material.

improvement.justification: SCAFFOLD comparisons, implementation links and expanded explanations provide useful improvements. However, v2 changes the trainable-method definitions without explaining their relationship to unchanged GH-OFL results, leaving unclear which formulation was evaluated. Figure 2 also newly labels NBdiag with pooled covariance despite the retained class-specific definition in the text. These method-to-evidence and consistency concerns make the net quality effect uncertain.
